messages:

Subject: Pilot for Optimize toolkit (batching/cache/quant) — pricing options

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Veridian is excited about the Optimize recommendations (especially the KV cache hints and batching suggestions). Before we commit resources for a proof-of-concept, procurement needs a clear pilot pricing/credit ask and an outline of the conversion incentives.

High level goals: reduce token $/op by >=25% on our RLHF scoring pipeline, verify end-to-end latency under 300ms p50 for live traffic, and have a small set of eval prompts to measure quality regressions after quantization.

Could you send a succinct pilot offer (credits, timeline, what you’ll measure, and any recommended quantization/batching presets to try)? Also flag any legal or procurement constraints we should be aware of.

Main contacts: me (Kayla), Sol (eng lead), and procurement@veridian.ai.

Thanks,
Kayla Chen
Head of ML Platforms | Veridian AI
[Attachment: veridian_pilot_requirements.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Chen <kayla@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot for Optimize toolkit (batching/cache/quant) — pricing options

Kayla — really appreciate the clear goals. Below is a compact pilot offer we can run next 6 weeks; happy to iterate.

Pilot: Efficiency Incentive (6 weeks)
- Upfront credits: 8,000 inference credits (usable for both hosted and dedicated trials).
- Performance-earned credits: up to +8,000 additional credits earned during the pilot — awarded in 2k increments each time we validate >=10% incremental token-cost reduction vs baseline (measured on agreed prompts).
- Conversion incentive: if Veridian converts to a 12-month committed capacity within 30 days of pilot close, we apply a conversion credit equal to 25% of pilot consumption (applied to first invoice).
- Discount: guaranteed 15% first-year discount on committed capacity for deals >$150k ARR (negotiable within the SOC2/enterprise guardrails).
- Observability add-on (optional): extended retention & eval dashboard for $3k/mo during pilot.

Technical guidance (what we'll test):
- Model variants: start with open-llama-70b-4bit-v2 (or equivalent quant-friendly variant you use).
- Quantization: begin with 4-bit quant + outlier-aware kernel; only move to aggressive 3-bit if quality unchanged on eval set.
- Batching: aim for variable batching with target latency SLO 300ms p50; configure batch windows at 12ms and adaptive concurrency to keep p95 under 800ms.
- KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts; expect >10% token savings on scoring workloads.

Attachments: redwood_pilot_scope.pdf (scope + metrics), pilot_credit_estimate.xlsx (cost math).

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, let me know the preferred start date and we’ll send a short MOP + statement of work.
2) We’ll schedule a technical kickoff with Sol and your infra lead.

I’ll loop in Neha (pricing) and Marissa (solutions) to align commercial language.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_pilot_scope.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot for Optimize toolkit — proposed credit structure (internal negotiation)

Folks — forwarding Kayla’s ask and the draft pilot offer below. Quick internal notes and proposed negotiation levers before I respond to procurement:

Summary of asks:
- Veridian wants clear pilot economics and conversion incentives tied to measured token-efficiency.

My recommended levers (conservative + creative):
1) Performance-earned credits (our innovation): keep the up-to-8k earned-credit structure. It encourages them to optimize and gives us measurable wins to showcase.
2) Upfront credits: 8k is reasonable for their volume; cap refunded credits to 50% of pilot consumption if they don’t convert.
3) Discount windows: 15% first-year is our baseline for mid-sized deals; we can move to 20% only if they commit to >=$200k ARR and provide a procurement-signed PO within 45 days.
4) Delivery SLA / credits: avoid custom SLA language in pilot MOP — instead offer a standard pilot MOP + 2-week hypercare. Legal will not approve bespoke uptime SLAs for pilots.
5) Technical guardrails: require that they run our recommended baseline quant/batch config first — we only consider deeper concessions if we see technical blockers.

Concession budget guidance for you, Neha: allow up to 12% additional discount (i.e., cap 27% total) in exchange for higher committed ARR and an accelerated PO. If we need to add more credits, prefer performance-conditional credits (ties to token-efficiency gains) rather than unconditional free credits.

Draft reply I want to send to Kayla is attached as a separate doc. Thoughts? I can soften the conversion terms if you think procurement will push back.

— Vivek

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Thanks Vivek — agree with the performance-earned-credit framing. A few legal/commercial points to incorporate into the external language:

- Procurement note: we can’t promise applied discounts until we have a signed order. Language should say "eligible for up to X% discount upon execution of a qualifying commit".
- No custom SLAs in MOP: include a 2-week hypercare window and standard platform uptime terms.
- Cap earned credit: define a clear measurement doc (our eval harness) and an objective party (Redwood runbook + Veridian metrics) to validate improvements.
- Pricing flexibility: I’ll authorize up to a 10% deepen on initial discount for legal-approved PO within 30 days. Anything beyond needs RevOps sign-off.

I’ve drafted cleaner external wording in the attached MOP language (mop_pilot_language.docx) and added the HubSpot link and the deal id to the header. Send externally once we’re aligned on the earned-credit metric buckets and conversion timeline.

— Neha

Kayla / Sol — thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Below is the agreed pilot offer and next steps (compact). This replaces earlier draft and reflects internal approvals.

Agreed pilot terms (Efficiency Incentive)
- Upfront credits: 8,000 inference credits (valid for 6 weeks).
- Performance-earned credits: up to 8,000 additional credits. Award schedule: +2,000 credits each verified time the pilot demonstrates >=10% token-cost reduction on the agreed eval suite (max 4 awards). Verification method: Redwood's eval harness + Veridian sampling (both parties sign verification note).
- Conversion incentive: if Veridian signs a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot close, Redwood will apply a conversion credit of 25% of pilot consumption to the first billed period.
- Discount eligibility: Veridian is eligible for up to 15% first-year discount on committed capacity; a deeper 25% discount requires >=$200k ARR and a PO within 45 days (per Neha’s guidance).
- Observability add-on: available during pilot for $3k/mo (optional).

Technical plan (we agreed during call):
- Start config: 4-bit quant + outlier-aware kernel; batching windows 12ms; KV prefix caching enabled for repeated scoring.
- Metrics: token $/op (primary), p50 latency (target <300ms), top-line eval quality on the shared prompt set (no >1% degradation expected when using 4-bit).

Attachments: redwood_pilot_scope.pdf, pilot_credit_estimate.xlsx, mop_pilot_language.docx

Next steps / timeline:
1) Veridian: confirm start date and sign the short MOP (I’ll send the DocuSign link once you confirm).
2) Redwood: schedule technical kickoff (1 hour) with Sol + infra lead — propose Friday 16 Apr 10:00 PT or Monday 19 Apr 09:00 PT.
3) Measurement: exchange eval prompts and baseline metrics within first 3 days of the pilot.

If that all looks good, I’ll send the MOP + DocuSign link and copy legal for a 72-hour turnaround on the pilot agreement.

Best,
